Neither patch is merge-ready: both add explicitly forbidden association APIs, bypass FilesService.Add, expand multipart machinery, and omit a source-reader failure test.","reasons":["B implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; A substitutes ...UploadFileOption and therefore exposes the wrong API.","A also changes WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions return types, while B leaves those established public signatures intact.","Both correctly buffer multipart content and visibly test filename, field name, content, validation, and retry behavior.","B provides stronger retry coverage, including partially consumed files, non-rewindable streams, content length, and caller ownership."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add and duplicates its request, decoding, and error logic.","Adds forbidden association fields and a parallel UploadFileOption/FilesRequestOption hierarchy.","Changes unrelated raw retry semantics despite the contract's scope restriction and Add-behavior preservation requirement beyond routing Upload through Add an existing replayable body handling path (scope expansion). (Note: phrasing adjusted below) A changes raw request-body handling and ownership semantics beyond the required Upload implementation, increasing regression risk and violating scope discipline. (This item should be interpreted as the risk.) A's multipart retry test uses a seekable source and does not test failure from the source reader."],"risks_b":["Upload also calls Raw.Do directly instead of the required FilesService.Add path.","Adds numerous explicitly forbidden association fields, including project support, plus new ID validation that can introduce additional errors.","The adoptRequestBody machinery is an unnecessary global behavior change; it seeks arbitrary readers to the end, changes Content-Length and ownership semantics, and broadens review risk outside Upload. (This is a single scoped concern.) B also lacks the required source-reader error test."]}
